name: New York
agency: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
permitAge: 16 (junior learner permit, Class DJ; MV-21 p. 6 and 11)

teen.supervisedHours: At least 50 hours of practice, including at least 15 after sunset, certified by a parent or guardian on form MV-262 given to the examiner at the road test (MV-21 p. 13-14); 10 hours in moderate to heavy traffic recommended
teen.holdPermit: Junior permit held at least six months, not counting time suspended or revoked, before the road test (MV-21 p. 14, 19)
teen.nightLimit: Junior permit: no driving 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. in New York City or Long Island; upstate only with parent, guardian or instructor (p. 12). Junior license: never drives in New York City; Long Island alone only directly to work/school etc.; upstate 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. alone only directly between home and work or a school course (p. 16)
teen.passengerLimit: Junior permit: only the supervisor in the front seat; no more than one passenger under 21 outside immediate family unless the supervisor is a parent, guardian or instructor (p. 13). Junior license: no more than one passenger under 21 unless immediate family (p. 15)
teen.phone: Junior permit or license: 120-day suspension on a texting or cell phone conviction (MV-21 p. 19); probationary license also 120 days. Second offense (revocation) is on the DMV web page, not in the handbook

bac.adult: 0.08 (DWI, p. 55); DWAI more than 0.05 up to 0.07 (p. 58); 0.18 aggravated DWI
bac.under21: 0.02 to 0.07 (Zero Tolerance; six-month suspension, p. 21 and 57)

notes: Handbook: Driver's Manual MV-21, no printed revision date; PDF created 2026-04-20. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers. Checked 2026-10-09 against the full text.
Written test: 20 questions, at least 14 correct, and at least 2 of the 4 road sign questions (MV-21 p. 10).

Class D permit test offered in 20 languages including Spanish, Chinese, Arabic and Haitian Creole; not Vietnamese or Tagalog (DMV permit test page, fetched 2026-10-09). School online test (OKTA) in English and Spanish (p. 10).
Supervisor must be 21 or older with a valid license for the vehicle, seated in front (p. 11). In NYC, junior permit daytime driving only with parent/guardian/instructor in a dual-control car (p. 12).
Most new drivers need a 5-hour pre-licensing course (MV-278) unless they complete a high school or college driver education course (p. 8, 13-14).
School bus: traffic from either direction stops, also across a divided highway; stay at least 20 feet back (p. 40).
No turn on red in New York City unless a sign allows it (p. 31).
Headlights required whenever wipers are needed for rain, snow, sleet or fog; daytime running lights do not count (p. 63).
55 mph when no limit is posted; 25 mph in New York City unless posted; some highways 65 (p. 47).
Move Over law covers emergency and hazard vehicles, and any vehicle stopped on the shoulder or road of a parkway or controlled-access highway (p. 35). The handbook gives no year for the expansion.
